As of 237 PM EST Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A well-defined, large upper level low pressure
system is currently swirling over northern Pennsylvania with
widespread showers on its northeast flank. With this system 
moving northeastward, it will bring these showers across our
region leading to certain rainfall areawide. Rain will be light
for the most part, with embedded somewhat heavier rainfall 
rates closer to 0.1"/hour, leading to additional rainfall widely
ranging from about 0.1" total to 0.25" in most locations. With
elongated surface low pressure area positioned near or just 
north of the International Border, this setup will aid in
greater rainfall amounts tending to be in our northern areas.
Additionally, as the low pressure departs overnight, a subtle
terrain-driven convergence and blocked flow will promote more
rain and high elevation snow in the early morning hours in
northwestern Vermont. Meanwhile, upslope westerly flow with 
moisture contribution from the eastern Great Lakes in northern 
New York also could bring additional light rain. Lack of any
cold air advection will limit snow accumulations to mainly
mountain summits during this period of upslope flow with snow
levels above 2500 feet. 

In contrast, the next round of widespread precipitation could
bring a little bit more wet snow for our region Saturday night
as snow levels fall into the 1500 to 2000 foot range. While 
snow amounts will not warrant any advisories and snow will not 
be widespread, this could be a sneaky hazardous event with
localized slick travel in our higher elevations for anyone 
traveling during this period. A subtle shortwave trough, 
lingering moisture, and some warm air advection will spark 
steady, light precipitation overnight. Then we should finally 
see a break in precipitation in our region on Sunday.

Then late Sunday night, a large area of rain will advance from
the west ahead of a seasonably strong area of low pressure
tracking northeastward, reaching western New York by daybreak.
Thereafter as this system reaches northern New York, most 
guidance suggests a rapid deepening of a secondary low to our
east. The combination of these systems will lead to a long
duration of rain during the day, between a steady widespread
rain and then potential for substantial upslope shower event
beginning in the afternoon from west to east. As temperatures
fall aloft, snow levels will fall steeply, likely down to about
1000 feet. As such, even valleys may see some snow with any 
accumulations driven strongly by elevation. The magnitude of large
scale westerly flow suggests flow will probably become 
unblocked quickly, favoring snow near mountain crests and
downwind. The expected gusty west winds are described in more 
detail below in Key Message 2.

KEY MESSAGE 2: As low pressure quickly intensifies passing east of 
Maine and ~1025mb surface high pressure building in the southern US, 
we'll have modest pressure gradients settling in. Mid-level cooling 
will result in steepening lapse rates as well, and we may have to 
monitor given 40-50 knot winds around 850mb. Surface wind gusts 
Monday night could reach up to 40 mph. These winds and steepening 
lapse rates should also support orographic precipitation. Some snow 
will be possible, mainly over higher terrain. Flow will likely be 
unblocked, and so summits and downwind will be favored for any 
potential light accumulations. Given flow will be unblocked, dry air 
is expected to quickly filter in.

Gradient flow will steadily relax, but still 15-25 mph gusts during 
the day on Tuesday and high temperatures in the 30s will feel 
chilly. Surface high pressure shifts northeast, and flow aloft 
becomes increasing zonal. This pattern favors dry and warm. By next 
Thursday, we'll be near 50 degrees during peak heating. It looks 
like there should be a weak cold front that tracks east Thursday 
evening into the overnight hours, but it will be more of a glancing 
blow. A few showers could take place with a brief cool down, but we 
will quickly switch back to deep southwest flow, and the latest NBM 
suggests Friday afternoon could end up being warmer anyway. Another 
weather system will approach towards next Saturday/Sunday.
